correctness.rationale: The divisor-cell adjacency criterion makes selected labels a chain; domination forces every selected cell to be taken whole and the chain to be maximal. Conversely maximality guarantees domination. Saturated chains are prime-factor words, yielding the polynomial. Adjacent totient-suffix swaps prove descending/ascending extremality, and the verifier exhaustively checks small actual graphs.
